contracts.docstring: Historical branch identity, with an unresolved repository represented explicitly as null.
Historical PR metadata whose repository binding is independent of its display name.
Close/abandon a pull request.
Read branches from one scoped repository snapshot; a supplied ID takes precedence over its display name.

Get the file tree for a repository at a given ref.

*ref* can be a branch name, tag, or commit SHA (7-40 hex chars).
Uses Forgejo when available, otherwise falls back to local git.
Read one file from the selected repository ID and project, using the same registration snapshot for local/remote resolution.
List Forgejo comments on a pull request.
Post a comment on a pull request via Forgejo.
Resolve historical PR browsing/comments by its bound repository, refusing unresolved labels instead of attaching a later namesake.
Capture the remote and path only after matching both recorded repository and project IDs.
Resolve a single project-bound registration, never substitute a same-named source when an explicit ID is missing.
Capture local path and remote URL together so later name reuse cannot split one read across repositories.
Choose transport from one already-scoped registration snapshot without another name-based database lookup.
Restore schema66 only with no branch/PR history and no later schema; populated installations use forward repair or backup.
Read and annotate stored branch history without inferring native ownership, acceptance or permission to mutate Git.
Annotate only a repository-scoped historical branch; this metadata never executes Git or grants native acceptance.
Update only the historical row matching the supplied project, repository and branch label.
Annotate one bound historical branch without inferring deletion permission from its age or name.
Retain other projects' and repositories' namesakes while recording this explicit annotation.
Preserve imports without reviving a second executor, unchecked checkout merge or destructive cleanup path.
Accept the historical constructor without resolving paths, discovering Git or creating directories.
Refuse legacy workspace setup before mkdir; native allocations are recorded before filesystem work.
Refuse reusing an old agent directory or branch as a new execution attempt.
Refuse both ordinary and forced removal without pretending a failed deletion succeeded.
Refuse inferred filesystem ownership from an agent label; use scoped retained-material controls.
Refuse the obsolete ambient Git reader instead of hiding unavailable history as an empty list.
Refuse unchecked merging into the current checkout; publication requires exact source, destination and receipt.
Refuse bulk cleanup; preservation and retention decisions belong to explicit owner operations.
Refuse batch allocation through the removed TUI engine before any directory or process is created.
Read and annotate historical PR records without treating status or actor labels as native acceptance/publication authority.
Annotate one historical PR and its bound branch atomically; names cannot transfer ownership or authorize Git effects.
Resolve the original row under the write lock and retain its event with both scoped metadata changes.

Derive ``{owner}/{repo}`` from the repository's ``remote_url``.

Parses both HTTPS (``https://host/owner/repo.git``) and SSH
(``git@host:owner/repo.git``) URL formats.
Read the legacy caller's remote inside its explicit project and repository-name scope.
Decode a previously selected registration's remote without re-resolving its mutable display name.
Keep import compatibility while rejecting obsolete database-backed worktree effects before any IO.
Refuse per-agent reuse/reset; native preparation admits an independent allocation for each exact attempt.
Refuse force removal and false removed-state updates; retained dirty/untracked files remain untouched.
Refuse age/roster-based disposal and pruning; missing actors do not establish that their work is dispensable.
Bind admitted selection to one original acquisition receipt; no new persistence table, execution controller or model loop.
List scoped historical branch records; stored commit hashes are suggestions, not live Git observations.
Freeze only the actual scoped record and owner-chosen immutable commit; original context and bytes are not guessed at admission.
Correlate historical PR/task/repository/worktree labels without reading Git, inferring byte availability or transferring old approval to native work.
Seed two independent repositories with deliberately identical human-readable names.
A PR without a matching branch in its own repository cannot adopt another project's same-named history.
Two projects may retain app/task/1; owner closure changes exactly one branch and publishes one transactional event.
A failed durable event cannot leave a closed review or abandoned branch behind.
A later repository named app cannot receive closure, navigation or prior-code selection intended for the original ID.
Actual Git reads use the selected ID even after its name is reused, and never fall back after a foreign or missing ID.
Historical remote comments remain bound to the original repository rather than a replacement sharing its old display name.
Absence of an original repository ID remains explicit, including before any legacy remote request.
Fail if a missing historical association reaches remote resolution by display name.
Old unscoped calls cannot silently mutate every namesake; explicit matching identities affect one row.
Migration67 keeps original rows and deleted-ID history while resolving only existing scoped registrations.
An unused schema67 can return to66 without dropping unrelated project data or bypassing later-schema guards.
Unused schema66 reverses safely; any admitted operation prevents erasing its recovery history.
Even force cleanup or an explicit merge target refuses before touching a real dirty checkout or launching Git.
Detect ambient execution from an obsolete TUI path, regardless of requested destination.
Create a real linked checkout with tracked and untracked owner edits before testing retired entry points.
Every historical mutation refuses before any Git process or database callback, leaving real edits and records intact.
Detect any attempt to reactivate the obsolete process or persistence path.
Actual Git must stay unchanged despite a legacy approved label or a PR with another task/project identity.
Fresh authoring and explicit prior-code reuse keep original receipts, independent checks/review and an unchanged source.
Only the accepted candidate head and stable marker enter the source; its checked-out branch/files remain at the original base.

scope: New/changed Python definitions and modules in this delivery. Relevant new frontend modules and exported helpers also carry English JSDoc; no claim that all historic project definitions are documented.
